extracted.intended_audience: PTAB members, USPTO employees, patent practitioners, and parties to PTAB proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedures and criteria governing (1) convening a Precedential Opinion Panel to establish binding agency authority, (2) nominating and reviewing issued Board decisions for designation as Precedential or Informative, and (3) de-designation and publication of such decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for Precedential Opinion Panel review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Precedential Opinion Panel generally will be used to establish binding agency authority concerning major policy or procedural issues, or other issues of exceptional importance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples given include addressing constitutional questions; important issues regarding statutes, rules, and regulations; important issues regarding binding or precedential case law; issues of broad applicability to the Board; resolving conflicts between Board decisions; promoting certainty and consistency; or rehearing any case the Panel determines warrants attention. The Panel is for limited situations where it is appropriate to create binding agency authority through adjudication before the Board.

rubrics_metrics.name: Composition of the Precedential Opinion Panel and delegation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: By default the Precedential Opinion Panel shall consist of the Director, the Commissioner for Patents, and the Chief Judge; the Director selects members and may determine that a panel of more than three members is appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may replace default members with the Deputy Director, Deputy Chief Judge, or an Operational Vice Chief Judge. The three primary members may delegate their authority in the following order: Director first, then Commissioner for Patents, then Chief Judge. Delegated authority may be assigned, based on availability, to the Deputy Director; the Deputy Chief Judge; or an Operational Vice Chief Judge in order of seniority. No individual may receive the delegated authority of more than one member. Reasons for delegation include conflicts of interest, availability, or when issues are directed to procedural aspects of practice before the Board. (Also notes that 35 U.S.C. §6(c) requires at least three Board members hear proceedings.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods for obtaining Precedential Opinion Panel review
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director may convene a Precedential Opinion Panel sua sponte in his or her sole discretion; additionally, any party to a proceeding or certain Board members may recommend Panel review following specified submission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
Any party may recommend Panel review by emailing Precedential_Opinion_Panel_Request@uspto.gov and must accompany the email with a rehearing request filed with the Board that satisfies 37 C.F.R. § 41.52(a) or 42.71(d), including applicable due dates. The email must identify with particularity the reasons for recommending review and must include counsel for all other parties as recipients. The email must contain at least one of the specified statements of counsel at the beginning (provide specific-citation templates):
- "Based on my professional judgment, I believe the Board panel decision is contrary to the following decision(s) ... (cite specific decisions)."
- "Based on my professional judgment, I believe the Board panel decision is contrary to the following constitutional provision, statute, or regulation: (cite specific provision, statute, or regulation)."
- "Based on my professional judgment, I believe this case requires an answer to one or more precedent-setting questions of exceptional importance (set forth each question in a separate sentence)." 
Other Board members (including Commissioner for Patents and Chief Judge, and any other member) may also recommend Panel review by email, provided the recommendation complies with the due dates in 37 C.F.R. §§ 41.52(a) or 42.71(d). There is no right to further review of a recommendation not granted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Screening Committee membership and role
rubrics_metrics.description: A Screening Committee will review recommendations for Precedential Opinion Panel review and forward its recommendations to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Screening Committee is comprised of the members of the Precedential Opinion Panel, or their designees, typically in equal numbers (for example, 3 designees of each of the Chief Judge, Commissioner for Patents, and Director). Designees must be USPTO employees with a legal degree selected from: PTAB Administrative Patent Judges; the Deputy Director; individuals with a grade of SES or SL reporting (directly or indirectly) to certain Patent-related Deputy Commissioners; or attorneys reporting (directly or indirectly) to the General Counsel or Solicitor. The Committee forwards recommendations to the Director, who, where appropriate, will convene a Precedential Opinion Panel.

rubrics_metrics.name: Precedential Opinion Panel review procedures and authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: When convened, the Precedential Opinion Panel will enter an order notifying parties and the public, identify the issues to be resolved and the panel composition, and will render a decision resolving the identified issues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Panel may request additional briefing, may authorize the filing of amicus briefs in appropriate circumstances, and may order an oral hearing at its discretion. The Panel maintains authority over all issues while the case is under review but may delegate authority back to the prior Board panel to handle routine interlocutory matters, conference calls, or other matters outside the intended scope of the Panel review; if delegated, the prior panel must keep the Panel apprised and provide reasonable prior notice of any intended decision. If further proceedings are warranted after the Panel decision, the prior Board panel typically will conduct those proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication, labeling, and effect of Precedential Opinion Panel decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Precedential Opinion Panel decisions will, unless designated otherwise by the Panel, set forth binding agency authority and shall be labeled and published according to procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Director may designate any decision as precedential without regard to these procedures, but Precedential Opinion Panel decisions designated as precedential shall be labeled "Precedential," posted to the Board’s Precedential Decisions Web page, and may be sent to commercial reporters. The Panel may alternatively designate its decision as routine (if no longer precedent-setting) or as informative (if it meets criteria for informative decisions). Panel opinions may be de-designated under the de-designation procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating process and substantive criteria for designating an issued decision as Precedential
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person (including Board members, USPTO employees, and members of the public) may nominate a routine decision for designation as precedential; nominations must set forth particular reasons and identify any conflicting Board decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nominations should be submitted by email to PTAB_Decision_Nomination@uspto.gov and must identify with particularity the reasons for designation and any other Board decisions that may be in conflict. Reasons for precedential designation are generally the same as criteria for invoking the Precedential Opinion Panel: constitutional questions; important issues regarding statutes, rules, and regulations; important issues regarding binding or precedential case law; issues of broad applicability to the Board; resolving conflicts between Board decisions; and promoting certainty and consistency among Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nominating process and substantive criteria for designating an issued decision as Informative
rubrics_metrics.description: A routine decision may be nominated for informative designation when it provides guidance or norms to the Board without being binding authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of reasons for informative designation include: (1) providing Board norms on recurring issues; (2) providing guidance on issues of first impression to the Board; (3) providing guidance on Board rules and practices; and (4) providing guidance on issues that may develop through analysis of recurring issues in many cases (e.g., factors to consider on institution decisions). Nominations must be submitted to PTAB_Decision_Nomination@uspto.gov with particularized reasons and identification of any conflicting decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive Judges Committee composition, Board review period, and recommendation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Nominated decisions that pass initial screening are further reviewed by an Executive Judges Committee which recommends to the Director whether to designate a decision as precedential or informative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Judges Committee consists of five members and includes the Chief Judge, the Deputy Chief Judge, and the Operational Vice Chief Judges, in order of seniority and availability. As part of evaluation, the Committee may solicit and review comments from all Board members during a Board review period (typically five business days). Any Board member may submit written comments during that period; the Committee may share comments with all Board members. After the review period, the Committee compiles and evaluates comments and determines by majority vote whether to recommend designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Director approval, notification, confidentiality handling, and publication of designated decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: No decision or portion thereof may be designated as precedential or informative under these procedures without the Director’s approval; once approved, the decision is published, labeled, dated, and disseminated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Executive Judges Committee submits its recommendation and explanation to the Director, who may consult with others (e.g., members of the Precedential Opinion Panel or Office of the General Counsel). If the Director approves, the Director will notify the Chief Judge. If the decision would otherwise be confidential because a patent application is preserved in confidence under 35 U.S.C. § 122(a), publication or dissemination follows notice and opportunity for written objection afforded by 37 C.F.R. § 1.14. Designated decisions or portions thereof shall be labeled "Precedential" or "Informative," include the date of designation, indicate designated portions if applicable, be posted electronically on the Board’s Precedential and Informative Decisions Web page, and may be sent to commercial reporters that publish Board decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effect of precedential versus informative designations
rubrics_metrics.description: A precedential decision is binding Board authority in subsequent matters involving similar facts or issues; an informative decision sets forth Board norms but is not binding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Informative decisions "should be followed in most cases, absent justification," but do not have binding authority. A decision previously designated under a prior version of SOP 2 remains designated unless de-designated under the de-designation procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure and grounds for de-designating a precedential or informative decision
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person may suggest that a designated decision should no longer be designated, and nominations for de-designation should be submitted with particularity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Grounds for de-designation include the decision being rendered obsolete by subsequent binding authority, inconsistent with current policy, or no longer relevant to Board jurisprudence. Nominations for de-designation should be sent to PTAB_Decision_Nomination@uspto.gov. If the Director determines the decision should no longer be designated, the Chief Judge will notify the Board, the decision will be removed from the Board's Precedential and Informative Decisions Web page, and the public will be notified that the decision has been de-designated. No decision will be de-designated without Director approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication obligation and definition of "decision" under the SOP
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrative Procedure Act requires agencies to make available final opinions and orders; the SOP defines the Board's practice for publishing decisions and defines what constitutes a decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Since August 1997, most final Board decisions have been made available electronically. A 'decision' for purposes of this SOP refers to any Board decision, opinion, or order, or the rehearing decision of any Board decision, opinion, or order. A routine decision is binding in the case in which it is made even if not designated as precedential or informative, but is not otherwise binding authority. Electronic publication of most decisions depends on whether the underlying application is entitled to confidentiality under 35 U.S.C. § 122; only a relatively small number of decisions remain confidential.
